name: Albania: Tirana, the Accursed Mountains, Berat, Gjirokastër

cities.base: The blocks between Skanderbeg Square, the Pyramid and Blloku. Everything you will do on foot is inside a twenty minute triangle, the food and the bars are in Blloku and around Pazari i Ri, and you avo
cities.name: Tirana

cities.base: Nobody needs a night here. It is 35km north of Tirana, 50 minutes up a hairpin road, and it is a half day at most. If you are driving north to Shkodër anyway it is a legitimate stop rather than a sepa
cities.name: Krujë

cities.base: There is nothing at Koman but a dam, a tunnel and a jetty, and nothing at Fierzë but a ramp. You sleep in Shkodër the night before, at 42.0693, 19.5033, because the minibus leaves there at 06:30 to me
cities.name: Lake Koman and the Fierzë crossing

cities.base: The strip of guesthouses along the valley road between Valbonë village and Rragam. Sleep as far up the valley as you can get, because the pass trailhead is at the top end and a bed at the bottom adds
cities.name: Valbonë

cities.base: There are no beds on the pass, only two seasonal coffee shacks. You sleep in Valbonë the night before and in Theth the night after, and your luggage goes round by road or stays where you started. This
cities.name: Qafa e Valbonës, the Valbonë to Theth pass

cities.base: The meadow around the church, between Okol at the top of the valley and the Grunas turning at the bottom. Everything in the valley is a walk from there, the guesthouses feed you, and you are ten minut
cities.name: Theth

cities.base: Mangalem, on the castle side of the Osum, or Gorica directly across the bridge. Both are five minutes from the water and fifteen from the castle gate. Gorica is quieter and gets the afternoon light on
cities.name: Berat

cities.base: No beds worth using. It is 45km southeast of Berat on a slow road, and the rafting operators collect you from your Berat guesthouse at about 08:00 and have you back by mid afternoon.
cities.name: The Osum canyon and Bogovë

cities.base: The old town above Çerçiz Topulli square, in the Palorto or Dunavat lanes. The whole upper town is stone stairs and cobbles, so book a guesthouse that will carry bags or park below and walk up with wh
cities.name: Gjirokastër

cities.base: A spring in a forest off the Gjirokastër to Saranda road, with a car park and a cafe and nothing else. One hour from Gjirokastër, 40 minutes from Saranda, and worth exactly the 45 minutes it takes if
cities.name: The Blue Eye at Muzinë

cities.base: Ksamil has thousands of beds and most of them sit behind concrete built without permits since 2015. You can sleep here, but on a ten day loop it is better as one long day from Gjirokastër: Butrint at
cities.name: Ksamil, Butrint and Saranda

cities.base: Between the Spile waterfront and Livadh, or up in Kastro, the old village on the hill. The waterfront is where the fish and the buses are; Kastro is 20 minutes of climbing above it and is where you wa
cities.name: Himarë

cities.base: A canyon mouth between Dhërmi and Vuno with a summer camp and a bar, no road to the sand and no reliable power. Park at the top, walk 30 minutes down, and leave before dark unless you have booked a te
cities.name: Gjipe beach and the canyon

cities.base: A 1,027m pass through black pine with the Ionian 1,000m straight below it. There are two hotels and a paragliding launch, and no reason to sleep here. It is 40 minutes north of Himarë and you drive ov
cities.name: The Llogara pass

places.name: Skanderbeg Square
places.note: Forty thousand square metres of stone from every region of the country, pedestrianised in 2017 and slightly domed so you cannot see the far side; the interest is the ring of buildings around it, Italian fascist, Ottoman and communist within one turn.

places.name: National History Museum
places.note: The mosaic on the facade is better than most of what is inside, but the Iliyrian rooms and the Communist Terror pavilion are worth the hour; English labelling thins out badly after the medieval floor.

places.name: Bunk'Art 1
places.note: Hoxha's five level anti nuclear command bunker, 106 rooms, opened to the public in 2014 and left cold and damp on purpose; bring a layer, bring cash, and allow the full two hours because there is no short route out.

places.name: Bunk'Art 2
places.note: Twenty four rooms under the Interior Ministry on the Sigurimi, the secret police, with the names of the executed on the walls; smaller and grimmer than Bunk'Art 1 and the better one if you only do a single bunker.

places.name: House of Leaves
places.note: The surveillance house itself, built as a maternity clinic in 1931 and used to bug the country until 1991, with the actual microphones and files on display; the quietest and most disturbing hour in the city.

places.name: The Pyramid of Tirana
places.note: Built in 1988 as Hoxha's mausoleum by his daughter, wrecked, squatted, and reopened in 2023 with staircases up the sloping sides; free to climb, open late, and the best thing to do at dusk in this city.

places.name: Dajti Ekspres cable car
places.note: Fifteen minutes and 800m up to a ridge with beech forest, a restaurant and the whole plain laid out; shut every Tuesday for maintenance and stopped in high wind, so check before you cross town.

places.name: Pazari i Ri
places.note: Rebuilt in 2017 with a tiled roof and a ring of restaurants, so it is half produce market and half dining terrace now; the fruit, honey and cheese stalls at the back are still the real thing and the byrek counters open at seven.

places.name: Mullixhiu
places.note: Bledar Kola cooks Albanian village food with technique, with a working flour mill in the entrance and a tasting menu around 30 euro; the one kitchen in the country you would book a month out, and it is closed Sundays.

places.name: Oda
places.note: Two small rooms hung with kilims doing tave kosi, fërgesë and stuffed peppers for about 10 euro a head; it has been in every guidebook for a decade and is still run by the same family and still honest.

places.name: Komiteti Kafe Muzeum
places.note: A room furnished entirely out of the 1970s with two dozen house rakis, mulberry through walnut, served in tiny glasses; it is a gimmick that works because the raki is genuinely good and the locals still outnumber the visitors.

places.name: Sky Tower revolving bar
places.note: The rotating floor has been unreliable for years, the drinks are double the city price and the glass is too dirty to photograph through; climb the Pyramid for free instead.

places.name: Krujë Castle and the Skanderbeg Museum
places.note: The castle held out against three Ottoman sieges under Skanderbeg; the museum inside it is a 1982 Pranvera Hoxha building full of copies rather than originals, and the ramparts and the view over the plain are the better half.

places.name: The Old Bazaar, Krujë
places.note: One cobbled street of wooden shopfronts, burned in 1967 and rebuilt, now selling the same carved chess sets and fake antiques in every doorway; good for a filigree pendant or a kilim if you bargain, otherwise twenty minutes.

places.name: Ethnographic Museum, Krujë
places.note: An intact 1764 Ottoman merchant house inside the castle walls with its olive press, hammam and loom still in place; a better hour than the Skanderbeg Museum next door and almost nobody goes in.

places.name: The Sari Salltik tekke
places.note: A Bektashi shrine in a cave on the mountain above the town, reached by a rough road then a stair; pilgrims come in August, the rest of the year you will have it to yourself and the view runs to the Adriatic.

places.name: The Koman ferry
places.note: Two and a half hours up a reservoir drowned in the Drin gorge, walls close enough on both sides that it reads as a fjord; the Berisha boat leaves Koman at 09:00 and Fierzë at 13:00 from roughly 15 April to 5 November, the smaller Dragobia runs year round and leaves Fierzë at 06:00.

places.name: The tunnel to the Koman jetty
places.note: Four hundred metres of unlit single lane rock tunnel with no pavement between the dam road and the boat ramp, shared by buses, cars and people carrying goats; it is genuinely alarming and it is also the only way through.

places.name: Fierzë ramp
places.note: A concrete ramp, a kiosk and a row of vans to Valbonë and Bajram Curri; there is nothing to do here except get into the right vehicle, and the drivers will find you before you find them.

places.name: Rilindja
places.note: The kitchen that started tourism in this valley in 2005 and still sets the standard: trout, cornbread, wild greens, honey from the slope behind; book the table when you book the bed because it fills with through hikers by 19:00.

places.name: The Valbonë riverbed
places.note: A kilometre wide bed of white boulders with a thin braid of water in summer and the whole thing in flood in May; you can walk out into the middle of it, and the scale of the walls only makes sense from there.

places.name: The walk up to Rragam
places.note: Four hours return on the valley road and track to the last hamlet and the pass trailhead, almost flat, shaded in the last hour; useful as a legs day before the pass and it shows you exactly where you will start.

places.name: The Kukaj valley waterfall
places.note: A steep side valley north of the road with a fall that runs hard in June and is a trickle by late August; the path is marked but faint in the upper meadow and you will meet shepherds rather than hikers.

places.name: Valbonë Valley National Park information point
places.note: A hut with a trail board and, in season, someone who actually knows whether the pass is clear and where the snow patches are; worth ten minutes the evening before you cross, and closed outside summer.

places.name: Dragobi and the Bajram Curri cave
places.note: The cave where Bajram Curri was cornered and killed by Zog's men in 1925, marked by a plaque above the road; ten minutes, and it explains why every second thing in this district carries his name.

places.name: The Shoshan canyon
places.note: A slot two metres wide and thirty deep cut into the plateau east of Bajram Curri, crossed by a plank bridge with no rail; a 45 minute drive from Valbonë and genuinely dangerous in wet weather.

places.name: The guesthouse table in Valbonë
places.note: Half board is how this valley works: soup, cheese, a meat dish and whatever was picked that morning, at 19:00 sharp for everyone at once; there is no menu, there is no card machine, and there is no ATM closer than Bajram Curri.

places.name: Bajram Curri town
places.note: A concrete district town 30 minutes down the valley with the last ATMs, pharmacy and supermarket before the mountains; not a sight, but plan a stop here or you will be paying for everything in whatever cash you brought.

places.name: The valley after dark
places.note: There is effectively no street lighting in the valley and the walls block what little glow comes from Kosovo, so the sky is as good as anywhere in the Balkans; the generators in some guesthouses cut out around 23:00, which helps.

places.name: Qafa e Valbonës
places.note: The saddle between the two valleys and the whole point of coming north; six to ten hours village to village with 850m up and about 1,050m down, and the descent on the Theth side is loose rock that wrecks knees more than the climb does.

places.name: The Rragam trailhead
places.note: Where the road ends and the red and white blazes start; guesthouses run a van up here for about 6 euro a head at 06:30 and 07:30, and taking it saves you 90 minutes of walking a gravel road in the dark.

places.name: The coffee shack at the pass
places.note: A wooden hut selling Turkish coffee, boiled eggs and warm cans, run only through the walking season; cash in lek or euro, no change for a 50, and it is the last water before the Theth side.

places.name: The kafe on the Theth descent
places.note: About two thirds of the way down, a family serve tea, raki and sometimes soup from a shed on the treeline; people stop here longer than they mean to, which is fine because Theth is only ninety minutes further.

places.name: The Theth church
places.note: A small stone Catholic church with a shingle bell tower, built in 1892, closed under the atheism law of 1967 and restored after 1991; it is the picture everyone takes and it takes about ten minutes.

places.name: The Lock-in Tower
places.note: A stone refuge where men under blood feud sat out the Kanun, sometimes for years, fed through a slot; one room, three metres of wall, and the clearest thing in the country about how the old law actually worked.

places.name: Grunas waterfall
places.note: Forty minutes up from the village on a rooty path to a 25m fall and a cold pool; a small landowner fee is collected at the gate in season, and the flow is strong in June and weak by September.
places.neighborhood: Grunas, south end of the valley

places.name: The Grunas canyon rim
places.note: A 60m slot the Shala river has cut below the waterfall path, with an unfenced viewpoint on a spur; go to the edge if you like, nobody will stop you, and there is no rail and no one to call.

places.name: The Blue Eye of Theth
places.note: A spring pool in a gorge an hour and a half above Nderlysë, reached on rock with fixed cable in two places; six hours return on foot from Theth, four if you pay for a 4x4 down the valley, and the last section is not for anyone unsure on their feet.

places.name: Nderlysë and the river pools
places.note: Six houses, a footbridge and a string of green rock basins in the Shala; the water is about 8C and people get in anyway, and there is one kitchen here doing trout for walkers coming off the Blue Eye path.

places.name: Qafa e Thorës
places.note: The last pass on the road in, with a cafe, a car park and the whole Theth basin opening below you; this is also the point that closes with snow and takes the village with it from about November to May.

places.name: Okol and the foot of Mount Arapi
places.note: Forty minutes up the valley to the last hamlet, under the 800m north face of Arapi that European climbers come here for; flat, easy, and the best evening light in the valley falls on that wall.

places.name: The climb toward Qafa e Pejës
places.note: The Peaks of the Balkans stage toward Montenegro, 1,000m of switchbacks to a notch in the wall with almost nobody on it; you need a border permit to go over, but you do not need one to climb to the pass and come back.

places.name: The old water mill
places.note: A stone mill on the stream below the church, restored and still turned on for visitors when the miller is about; twenty minutes, free, and it is on the way to everything else.

places.name: The guesthouse table in Theth
places.note: Half board again: corn bread, mountain cheese, lamb or beans, and a jug of raki that nobody asked for; guesthouses here are seasonal, most shut between late October and May, and none of them take cards.

places.name: Berat Castle
places.note: Thirteenth century walls with about forty households still living inside, chickens in the lanes and a dozen small Byzantine churches between the houses; the ramp up is steep, cobbled and slick, and a taxi to the gate costs about 3 euro.

places.name: Onufri Iconographic Museum
places.note: In the Cathedral of the Dormition, with the sixteenth century icons of Onufri, who used a red nobody has matched since, and a carved iconostasis that survived 1967 because the building was reclassified as a museum; winter hours drop to 16:00.

places.name: The Mangalem windows
places.note: The stacked Ottoman houses that give the town its nickname, best seen from the Gorica bank rather than from inside them; the lanes themselves are steep, narrow and full of people photographing other people's front doors.

places.name: Gorica and the old bridge
places.note: The Christian quarter across the Osum, joined by a seven arch stone bridge of 1780; quieter than Mangalem, colder in winter because the castle blocks the sun, and the right side of the river to be on at 19:00.

places.name: Ethnographic Museum, Berat
places.note: An eighteenth century house on the castle path laid out as a working Ottoman home, with the olive press, the loom and the sealed women's quarters; small, well done, and thirty minutes if you move.

places.name: The Church of the Holy Trinity
places.note: A fourteenth century cross in square church on a spur below the castle wall, usually locked, and the reason to walk out is the drop straight down to Gorica from beside it.

places.name: The King's Mosque and the Halveti teqe
places.note: A fifteenth century mosque with the Bektashi lodge behind it, whose carved and painted wooden ceiling is the best interior in the town and is almost always empty; dress covered and take your shoes off.

places.name: Solomoni Museum
places.note: Two rooms on Albania's Jewish history and on the Berat families who hid Jews under the besa obligation during the German occupation; short, unglamorous and worth the half hour.

places.name: Homemade Food Lili
places.note: Dinner in a family courtyard off the Mangalem lanes, four or five courses of whatever was cooked that day, and you must book, sometimes weeks ahead; closed Sundays and there is no sign on the door.

places.name: The Mangalemi terrace
places.note: A hotel terrace halfway up the castle path with the whole valley in front of it and competent grilled lamb and byrek behind it; you are paying for the view and the view is worth it at sunset.

places.name: Çobo Winery
places.note: Family winery twenty minutes out of town working Shesh i Bardhë and Shesh i Zi, the two grapes this region actually has; call ahead, the tasting is cheap, and the Kashmer red is the bottle to carry away.

places.name: The xhiro on Bulevardi Republika
places.note: From about 19:00 the whole town walks the length of the boulevard and back, which is the evening in every Albanian town and is free; sit outside a cafe with a macchiato and watch it instead of joining it.

places.name: The Osum canyon
places.note: Thirteen kilometres of limestone 60 to 80m deep, rafted in spring meltwater with grade 2 and 3 water and waterfalls coming in off the walls; outside March to May the river drops and it becomes a walk in a dry bed.

places.name: Bogovë waterfall
places.note: Twenty minutes on foot from the village through walnut trees to a cold spring fall with a pool you can get into; the village does trout and raki afterwards and takes cash only.

places.name: Mount Tomorr
places.note: The 2,416m ridge that closes the Berat skyline, with a Bektashi shrine near the summit and a pilgrimage every August; the access track needs a 4x4 and is impassable with snow from November to May.

places.name: Gjirokastër Castle
places.note: Five hundred metres of rampart, an artillery gallery of captured German and Italian guns, a clock tower, and an American T-33 that came down in 1957 and has been parked there ever since as a trophy; winter closing drops to 17:00.

places.name: The Cold War Tunnel
places.note: Eight hundred metres and 59 rooms dug in secret under the castle hill in the 1970s for the district leadership, opened in 2009; guided only, about 20 minutes, and cold enough that you will want a layer in August.

places.name: The Old Bazaar
places.note: Five stone streets of arcaded shopfronts rebuilt after the 1913 fire, now a mix of real workshops and souvenir stalls; the stone slab roofs above it are the thing to look at, and the cobbles are lethal in rain.

places.name: Skënduli House
places.note: A 1700s tower house with 64 windows and nine fireplaces, shown to you by the Skënduli who got it back after 1991 and who will tell you exactly what the state did with it in between; the best 45 minutes in town.

places.name: Zekate House
places.note: Twin towered, built 1811 for a vizier under Ali Pasha, with a painted first floor reception room that is the grandest interior in the town; self guided, and go before 16:00 because there is no lighting.

places.name: Ethnographic Museum, Gjirokastër
places.note: Built in 1966 on the site of the house Enver Hoxha was born in, which is the only reason it stands where it does; the contents are standard Ottoman domestic and the building's own story is the interesting part.

places.name: The Kadare house
places.note: Ismail Kadare's family house, burned in 1999 and rebuilt in 2016, with the cistern and cellar of Chronicle in Stone still there; worth it if you have read the book and thin if you have not.

places.name: Ali Pasha's bridge
places.note: Ninety minutes return from the castle gate on a dirt track to a stub of the aqueduct that fed the fortress, standing alone over a dry stream; almost nobody walks out, there is no shade, and it is the only quiet hour in the town.

places.name: Taverna Kardhashi
places.note: Qifqi, the fried rice and egg balls that only exist in this town, plus lamb with yogurt and good house red for about 10 euro a head; small, so it fills from 20:00 in summer.

places.name: Odaja
places.note: A stone room off the bazaar doing slow cooked lamb, oven vegetables and Gjirokastër style trahana; steady rather than exciting, and the one that still has a table when the others do not.

places.name: Te Kubé
places.note: A cafe and bookshop under the 1757 mosque with proper coffee, cake and a shaded terrace; the useful stop between the castle and the upper houses when the stone gets too hot to climb.

places.name: Antigonea
places.note: The city Pyrrhus founded and Rome destroyed in 167 BC, on a ridge 30 minutes east of town, with foundations, a stoa and nobody there; go for the emptiness and the view, not for standing walls.

places.name: The Blue Eye at Muzinë
places.note: A karst spring over 50m deep pushing out water at about 10C, with a viewing platform and a 2km walk in from the car park; swimming is now banned under its natural park status, which removes most of the reason people used to come.

places.name: The riverside cafe below the spring
places.note: Tables on decking over the outflow under plane trees, fifteen degrees cooler than the road, doing coffee and grilled trout; it is the better half of the stop and almost everyone walks straight past it.

places.name: Butrint
places.note: Greek, Roman, Byzantine and Venetian layers on a wooded peninsula between a lake and a channel, excavated by Ugolini in the 1920s; be at the gate at 08:30, because the Corfu day boats land around 10:00 and the site is a single one way loop.

places.name: The theatre and baptistery at Butrint
places.note: A third century BC theatre that usually has water in the orchestra, and a sixth century baptistery whose mosaic floor is kept buried under sand for its own protection and uncovered only rarely; ask at the ticket desk whether it is open.

places.name: The triangular fort on the Vivari channel
places.note: Ali Pasha's fort at the channel mouth, reached by a small boat from the Butrint side for a couple of euro; twenty minutes of ruin and an hour of not being in the crowd.

places.name: The mussel farms on Lake Butrint
places.note: Shacks on stilts over the lake serving mussels pulled out of the water in front of you, grilled or in saganaki, for about 12 euro; this is the best meal in the south and it is ten minutes from the ruins.

places.name: The Ksamil islands
places.note: Four small islands a hundred metres offshore that you can swim or pedal to, with water as clear as the photographs suggest; get there before 10:00, because by midday the boats and the sunbed rows have taken the shoreline.

places.name: The Ksamil beach clubs
places.note: In July and August the public sand is gone under paid loungers at 25 to 40 euro a pair, the music runs from three sides at once, and the town behind is unpermitted concrete; drive twenty minutes to Pasqyra or go in June.

places.name: Pasqyra beach
places.note: A cove below the coast road with the clearest water on this stretch, reached down a long stair; it has sunbeds too but fewer of them, and the early morning hour before the road fills is the one to take.

places.name: Lekursi Castle
places.note: A sixteenth century fort on the hill with a restaurant inside it and Corfu straight across the water; the food is ordinary, the sunset is not, and you want to be up there by 19:00 in summer for a table.

places.name: The Saranda promenade
places.note: Two kilometres of seafront in front of a town that built too fast and too high, but the evening walk is real and the ice cream queues are locals; the town itself is not a reason to stay.

places.name: Himarë old town, Kastro
places.note: The Greek speaking village inside the old castle walls on the hill, half ruined, half restored into guesthouses, with two churches and a view down the whole coast; twenty minutes of climbing from the waterfront or five by car.

places.name: Spile beach
places.note: The town beach, five hundred metres of grey pebble with the promenade behind it and free stretches at both ends; convenient rather than beautiful, and fine for a swim before breakfast.

places.name: Livadh beach
places.note: A kilometre and a half of pebble with a gradual shelf, the easiest swimming near town and the one families use; the middle third is still free sand and the two ends are clubs at about 10 euro a pair of loungers.

places.name: Potami beach
places.note: Shallow and sheltered with a spring running in at one end that keeps the water cold; five minutes down the coast road and quieter than Livadh until about 11:00.

places.name: Llaman beach
places.note: A two hundred metre cove closed in by cliffs, down a steep track that puts most rental cars off; the least developed road accessible beach here and the reason to have a car at all.

places.name: Filikuri by boat
places.note: No road reaches it, so you go by boat from Spile or kayak round the headland, and there is a sea cave at one end big enough to swim into; boats leave about 10:00 in season and do not run in wind.

places.name: Porto Palermo castle
places.note: Ali Pasha's triangular fort on a causeway in a near circular bay, empty stone rooms and a roof you can walk; the submarine tunnel cut into the far side of the bay is still military and still closed.

places.name: Old Qeparo
places.note: The abandoned stone village two hundred metres above the new one, mostly roofless with a handful of houses brought back and one cafe; go at six, walk the lanes, and be down before the light goes because there is no lighting.

places.name: Dhërmi and Drymades
places.note: The longest good beach on this coast, with the old village up the slope above it and Drymades round the point; it is also where the festivals and the beach clubs are, so in August it is loud from noon until four in the morning.

places.name: Jale beach
places.note: A three hundred metre bay that has been sold entirely to two club operators with sound systems facing each other; the water is good and you will not hear yourself think, so go to Llaman instead unless you came to drink.

places.name: The fish on the Himarë waterfront
places.note: Whole fish sold by the kilo off ice at the front, grilled plain with lemon and oil; ask the price per kilo and the weight of your fish before it goes on the fire, every time, or the bill will surprise you.

places.name: Raki in Kastro at dusk
places.note: Two or three terraces among the ruins above the town, mulberry raki and olives, the sun going down into the Ionian behind Corfu; it closes out of season and the road up is single track with no passing places.

places.name: Gjipe beach
places.note: Three hundred metres of coarse sand where the canyon meets the sea, no road in, 30 minutes down from the car park and 45 back up; there is a bar and a campsite and the power is a generator, so bring cash and water.

places.name: The Gjipe canyon
places.note: An hour up a dry riverbed between 70m walls, scrambling over boulders, with climbers on bolted routes at the entrance; it floods after autumn storms and you should not be in it if rain is forecast.

places.name: The monastery above Gjipe
places.note: A ruined Orthodox monastery on the plateau where you leave the car, roofless and unsigned, with the whole bay under it; five minutes off the path and almost everybody walks past it.

places.name: The Llogara pass
places.note: The point where the road tops out and the Ionian appears a vertical kilometre below through black pine; there are lay bys and a paragliding launch, and in July the coaches queue at every one of them.

places.name: Qafa e Çezarit
places.note: The notch Caesar is said to have marched his legions through in 48 BC chasing Pompey, marked by a sign and a car park; the claim is thin and the view north over the Karaburun peninsula is not.

places.name: The Llogara pine forest
places.note: Marked paths through Bosnian and black pine bent flat by the wind off the sea, ten degrees cooler than the coast below; a good hour when the beaches are at their worst, and the only shade on this road.

outings.why: The whole centre is flat and walkable in a morning: the square and the History Museum, down the boulevard past the Pyramid to the House of Leaves, then Pazari i Ri for lunch and Blloku after dark. The heat in July and August is the only dif
outings.name: Tirana on foot: Skanderbeg Square, the Pyramid and Blloku
outings.season: All year. May, June, September and October are the sane mont
outings.fallback: Bunk'Art 2 and the House of Leaves back to back if it rains, both indoors and eight minutes apart.

outings.why: Both are on the eastern edge of the city and share a bus. Bunk'Art 1 is 106 rooms of Hoxha's command bunker under Mount Dajti and takes two hours; the cable car climbs 800m over the city from the same side. The cable car is shut on Tuesdays
outings.name: Bunk'Art 1 and the Dajti cable car
outings.season: All year. The cable car stops in high wind.
outings.fallback: Bunk'Art 1 alone, and the National History Museum in the afternoon.

outings.why: Fifty minutes north and 600m up to Skanderbeg's castle and the rebuilt bazaar. The Skanderbeg Museum is a Kristaqi and Pranvera Hoxha building from 1982 and is more interesting as architecture than as history. The bazaar is now mostly souve
outings.name: Krujë
outings.fallback: Skip it and go straight to Shkodër. It is the most missable thing in this plan.

outings.why: Minibus from Shkodër at 06:30, two hours to the dam at Koman, through a one lane unlit tunnel to the jetty, then 2.5 hours up a flooded gorge to Fierzë and a van on to Valbonë. It is the only way in and out of the far north without a five h
outings.name: The Koman ferry

outings.fallback: The road via Kukës and Bajram Curri, about five hours from Shkodër, if the boat is cancelled for weather.

destination.name: Albania: Tirana, the Accursed Mountains, Berat, Gjirokastër
destination.pitch: Two countries in one ten day loop: a limestone alpine north that is the real reason to come, and an Ottoman stone south that ends at a coast which is beautiful in June and unusable in August.
destination.caveat: Nothing here moves at the speed the map implies: Tirana to Gjirokastër is 230km and takes five hours, the Theth road is 70km of switchbacks, and the one day that decides the whole trip, the Valbonë to Theth pass, is under snow from roughly November to early June and the Koman ferry that feeds it onl Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Tirana is loud, half rebuilt and worth two nights for the museums and the food. It is not why you came.
because.food: Honest rather than refined: byrek, qofte, lamb in yogurt, fresh fish on the coast, and one genuinely good modern kitchen in Tirana. The wine is improving and still cheap.
because.nature: The Accursed Mountains are the last big unfarmed limestone range in Europe, and the Valbonë and Theth valleys sit under 2,500m walls with no road between them.
because.culture: Two intact Ottoman towns that UNESCO listed for their houses, a bunker museum under a mountain, and a dictatorship that ended within living memory and is still being argued about.
because.adventure: The pass at 1,795m, the canyon walk to the Theth Blue Eye, the Osumi in spring meltwater, and a ferry through a flooded gorge that carries livestock.
because.relaxation: A guesthouse terrace in Valbonë and a pebble cove south of Himarë in June. Not in August, and not on the driving days.
because.exploration: Half the country was sealed until 1991, the archaeology is unfenced, and most of what you walk past has no sign, no ticket and nobody at it.
